plain_english: What you see is the best rule found by searching 4607 valid strategy combinations on data the model had not seen — not a rule that passed an independent final exam. The crucial honesty point for this pair: semiconductors (SOX) and the broad market (SPY) move together about 71% of the time on the same day, but that is shared market exposure, NOT proof that semis predict the market. To test a real lead we required the signal to act at least one day AHEAD and to beat a trivial 'follow SPY's own trend' rule. It did edge SPYs own momentum on Sharpe, but the win is fragile: the rule looked WORSE than buy-and-hold in its training years, only shone in a single strong-semis stretch (2021-2026), lost money in every past crisis (Dot-Com, GFC, COVID), and most rules we tried scored below buy-and-hold. So this is a search-found pattern, not a confirmed edge. Lead-lag statistics: Bidirectional Granger (both directions significant) — feedback, not clean lead — note the relationship runs BOTH ways (semis and the market push each other), so it is feedback, not a one-way lead.
